requirements.requirement: Planter for a sunny kitchen windowsill
requirements.evidence: Three interconnected bins (bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full, bin:0,-1,0~hex-bin-full, bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full) on low 3-cell base (pieces 0,0,0 / 1,0,0 / 0,-1,0) - compact ~330mm long windowsill trough, open-top bins filled with soil for growing. Sunny location is siting; shape is low, open planter suitable for sun.
Soil-filled bins planted: prop:1 basil-young in 0,0,0, prop:2 parsley-young in 0,-1,0, prop:3 mint-young in 1,0,0 - three distinct herb plants verified by look and check_build clear.

finish.summary: Built compact 3-cell windowsill planter with three full-depth bins, each filled with soil and planted with a herb (basil, parsley, mint). Caps and joint bolts applied, mesh clear.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: Sunny herbs on the way — I'll set up your windowsill planter for three.
